 Judgment

The insurer is in appeal challenging the liability fixed on it to pay the compensation awarded by the Member, MACT-II, Yadgiri (henceforth referred as 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.107/2015, vide judgment and award dated 28.03.2017.
2.

A claim petition filed by respondent No.1 herein under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 was entertained by the Tribunal and compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- was awarded.

The insurer of the offending vehicle was directed to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the insurer is in appeal.

3. Learned counsel for the insurer contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was authorized only to drive a light motor vehicle (non-transport) and therefore, he was not authorized to drive a passenger vehicle.
Learned counsel NC: 2023:KHC-K:1211 therefore, contended that the insurer was not liable to pay compensation.

4. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that the ground urged by the insurer is squarely covered by the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs.
Oriental Insurance Company Limited1.

entities.text:
Mukund Dewangan Vs.
Oriental Insurance Company Limited1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. The question whether a person licenced to drive a light motor vehicle (non-transport) is also entitled to drive a light motor vehicle (transport) and the question whether in such situation, the insurer can claim exoneration from the liability to pay the compensation is fully covered by the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra) where the Apex Court held that the insurer was not exonerated.
In view of the above, nothing survives for consideration in this appeal and therefore, the appeal is dismissed.
Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
